rulings.challenge_claim: The unit's statement that 19:15 restates the coming ruin rather than repeating the jar-oracle's own wording is byte-false; the cohesion binding 19:15 back across the unit's own opening seam goes undisclosed; and the setumah cited at 19:14 is a break dividing the span's two verses.
rulings.grounds: Two arms hold; the first is overstated and carries a tier error of its own. The divine-title stack does stand at both ends of the ch-19 complex, יְהוָ֨ה צְבָא֜וֹת אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל (oshb:Jer.19.3, byte tier) and יְהוָ֤ה צְבָאוֹת֙ אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל (oshb:Jer.19.15, byte tier), but the two runs are not byte-identical: the 19:3 run collates against 19:15 at accent_stripped tier only, three of its four words differing in cantillation. Tier-1 (divine-title formula), recurrence at accent_stripped tier. The construction arm does not reach 19:15 either: a contiguous consonantal sweep of the hinneni-plus-participle run returns 7 verses (sweep: 7 verses: 5:15, 11:11, 19:3, 31:8, 35:17, 45:5, 49:5) and excludes 19:15, because the ketiv/qere pair מבי מֵבִ֜יא (oshb:Jer.19.15, byte tier) stands there, its unpointed ketiv breaking the run between the two words. And 19:15's own clause כָּל הָ֣רָעָ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר דִּבַּ֖רְתִּי עָלֶ֑יהָ (oshb:Jer.19.15, byte tier) is a back-reference in summary form, so the unit's sentence is an overstatement rather than a falsehood. What is upheld, and is the load-bearing finding, is the cohesion arm: the stack the unit files as its own opening evidence stands twelve verses earlier inside the unit this row is cut away from, so a byte-true device straddles this row's own seam at 19:13|19:14 undisclosed, arguing continuity against the cut until it is disclosed. The parashah arm is upheld as stated: the inventory records SAMEKH at Jer.19.14, a break after that verse, which divides this two-verse span between its two verses, while the field states it as a mark carried by the row's own opening verse with that internal force unstated - and four sibling spans in the same part use the within-the-span wording for the same configuration (single-witness, tier-3 weak, never a driver). New finding: the inventory records a ketiv/qere at Jer.19.15 (1 note) sitting on the participle inside the very construction the non-repetition sentence turns on; neither the Hebrew nor the English quote reaches it, so the declared queue arms are confirmed false positives on quote-binding, but the verse's content is argued in prose and the variant is disclosed nowhere in the row.
rulings.remedy: boundary_rationale: replace the clause asserting that 19:15 restates the ruin rather than repeating the jar-oracle's own wording with a sentence that discloses the recurrence - the same divine-title stack opens the valley proclamation at 19:3 and the temple-court proclamation at 19:15 (recurrence at accent_stripped tier, tier named in-field), and 19:15 refers back to the evil already pronounced. device_notes: (a) state that the SAMEKH recorded at Jer.19.14 falls after that verse and therefore divides this two-verse span, using the same within-the-span wording the sibling spans use; (b) disclose the ketiv/qere at Jer.19.15 (single-witness). Test the cure must pass: the rewritten sentence must survive the check that killed the original - a contiguous consonantal sweep of the cited construction returns 7 verses and does not include 19:15, so no wording may assert byte-level or contiguous recurrence at that verse, and every recurrence claim in the field must name the tier it collates at.

rulings.challenge_claim: The rejected alternative tests a weaker internal rival than the unit's own disclosed evidence supports, and the byte-true renaming catchword straddling the closing seam at 20:6|20:7 goes undisclosed.
rulings.grounds: The first arm is upheld cleanly. The alternative weighed is the day-change split at 20:2|20:3, but the disclosed petuchah falls after 20:3 and 20:4 opens verse-initially on כִּ֣י כֹ֣ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֡ה (oshb:Jer.20.4, byte tier), a ki-subordinated messenger-formula restart. A tier-1 speech-formula restart and the tier-3 substrate break (single-witness, never a driver) coincide at 20:3|20:4, a juncture the field leaves untested, while the rival it does test carries neither signal. The ki subordinates the oracle to the renaming that grounds it, so the span itself is not in doubt; the defect is in the field's choice of rival. The second arm holds substantively but is mislabeled twice. The renaming run מָג֥וֹר מִסָּבִֽיב (oshb:Jer.20.3, byte tier) and the taunt מָג֣וֹר מִסָּבִיב֒ (oshb:Jer.20.10, byte tier) are not byte-identical: they collate at skeleton tier, the accents differing at both words. The two-word phrase is a 5-verse object at consonantal tier (sweep: 5 verses: 6:25, 20:3, 20:10, 46:5, 49:29), two of whose members sit either side of the seam this row closes at, so the cross-seam cohesion finding stands - at skeleton tier, not byte. And לְמָג֜וֹר (oshb:Jer.20.4, byte tier) is a bare prefixed noun, not a member of the two-word phrase object; counting it as a third member of that object blends two count objects in one digit.
rulings.remedy: strongest_rejected_alternative: replace the day-change rival with the 20:3|20:4 rival and state the ground for declining it - the ki subordinates the oracle to the renaming it grounds. device_notes: disclose that the renaming phrase at Jer.20.3 recurs at Jer.20.10, outside this span and across its closing seam, naming the tier (skeleton) and naming the object as the two-word phrase (sweep: 5 verses); keep the bare prefixed noun at Jer.20.4 as its own separate object if it is cited at all. Test the cure must pass: the rewritten alternative must name a rival that carries a disclosed substrate break or a tier-1 device at the juncture it tests, and no recurrence sentence may say byte-identical for a pair that collates at skeleton.

rulings.challenge_claim: The stated ground for declining the split at 20:13|20:14 is contradicted by the bytes of 20:13; the confession-cycle digit is put in sweep shorthand for a set no sweep produces; and the taunt at 20:10 straddles the row's opening seam undisclosed.
rulings.grounds: The first arm is real but positionally loose. The imperative pair שִׁ֚ירוּ לַֽיהוָ֔ה הַֽלְל֖וּ אֶת יְהוָ֑ה (oshb:Jer.20.13, byte tier) stands at 20:13's own opening, so it marks 20:12|20:13, not the declined pivot at 20:13|20:14. What does stand at the declined pivot is an addressee change - 20:12 addresses the deity directly, 20:13 addresses a plural audience with the divine name as the object of its verbs, and 20:14 is an addressee-less curse - together with the SAMEKH the unit itself discloses at Jer.20.13, a break after that verse falling precisely at the pivot the field declines and left unweighed in that field (single-witness, tier-3 weak, never a driver). So the ground as written overstates the pivot's unmarkedness, though not for the reason given. The frontier flag and the held-open statement mitigate the boundary risk but do not repair the ground. The type point is upheld: 20:13 is a hymnic call to praise folded into a span typed as a confession, with no operative-category deviation note, which the closed vocabulary requires wherever a span's bytes deviate from its declared type. The second arm is upheld: the five-span citation puts an editorially enumerated set into the one sanctioned citation shorthand. Sweeps over this corpus return verse or token counts of a named object; confession delimitation is not a byte-swept object and no such object exists in the staged device inventory. The enumeration is standard, its provenance misstated. The third arm is upheld substantively with the same tier correction as the neighbouring span: מָג֣וֹר מִסָּבִיב֒ (oshb:Jer.20.10, byte tier) and the renaming at 20:3 collate at skeleton, not byte, and the phrase is a 5-verse object (sweep: 5 verses: 6:25, 20:3, 20:10, 46:5, 49:29) straddling this row's opening seam at 20:6|20:7 undisclosed.
rulings.remedy: strongest_rejected_alternative: restate the ground so it survives the pivot's own bytes - name the addressee change across 20:12-20:14 and the disclosed break after Jer.20.13, then give the reason the pivot is still declined (no tier-1 onset opens 20:14: no messenger formula with a frame-owner change, no discourse-frame imperative, no scene or date frame) and keep the internal edge held open. boundary_rationale: remove the sweep shorthand from the confession-cycle enumeration - state the enumeration plainly with no sweep citation, or replace it with a digit-bearing sweep over a named byte object with its unit named. device_notes: add the one-sentence operative-category deviation note for the hymnic call at Jer.20.13 inside a confession-typed span, and disclose the renaming phrase recurring at Jer.20.3 across this row's opening seam (sweep: 5 verses; skeleton tier). Test the cure must pass: the rewritten ground must not assert the absence of a signal the pivot verse's bytes carry, the disclosed break at Jer.20.13 must be weighed in the same field that declines the pivot, and the sweep shorthand must cite a byte-swept object with its unit named.

rulings.challenge_claim: 21:1 is called a dated header although its temporal element is an occasion clause and the site stands outside the classified date census, and the addressee assigned to the 21:4-21:7 answer is not the one the bytes name.
rulings.grounds: Both arms verified on bytes. The header at 21:1 is a genuine member of the eleven-verse prose-sermon superscription shape, so the parent flip at this verse is tier-1 warranted and the row does not straddle it. But its temporal element is בִּשְׁלֹ֨חַ אֵלָ֜יו הַמֶּ֣לֶךְ צִדְקִיָּ֗הוּ (oshb:Jer.21.1, byte tier), a bet-prefixed infinitive construct naming an occasion: no year word, and not the bet-plus-cardinal shape. The classified date census carries 19 candidate sites (sweep: 19 sites) and 21:1 is not among them; the row's own filed signal list carries no date key, and the rendered header carries no date either. A dated royal embassy therefore overshoots the bytes, the census, and the row's own signals. On the addressee: 21:3 reads כֹּ֥ה תֹאמְרֻ֖ן אֶל צִדְקִיָּֽהוּ (oshb:Jer.21.3, byte tier), naming Zedekiah as the one to be told, and the oracle body then speaks in the plural to those holding the weapons, אֲשֶׁ֣ר בְּיֶדְכֶם֒ אֲשֶׁ֨ר אַתֶּ֜ם נִלְחָמִ֣ים בָּ֗ם (oshb:Jer.21.4, byte tier). The named messengers are couriers, not the addressee, so the rejected alternative's warrant - that 21:8 shifts the address from the king's own messengers to the people at large - mis-names its point of departure. The seam at 21:7|21:8 survives on the byte-true fresh commission at 21:8; only the stated warrant fails. The identical mis-naming stands as the seam warrant of the adjacent span at 21:8-21:10, so this is one wording defect across two units, not two independent ones.
rulings.remedy: boundary_rationale: drop the dated characterisation of the 21:1 header and describe the temporal element as an occasion clause (the king's sending), unless a year element is shown in the verse's own bytes - there is none; do not add a date_frame key to observed_substrate_signals. strongest_rejected_alternative: correct the point of departure - the address at 21:3-21:7 is to Zedekiah and, in the plural, to the city's defenders, and 21:8 turns it to the people at large. Apply the identical correction to the same warrant sentence in the adjacent span at 21:8-21:10 as one edit, not two. Test the cure must pass: no field may assign a date classification to a site absent from the 19-site census (sweep: 19 sites) or lacking a year element in its own bytes, and the corrected addressee sentence must name the party the relay clause at 21:3 names.

rulings.challenge_claim: The addressee the seam warrant turns on is mis-named, the English gloss drops the formula its own Hebrew run carries, and an unflagged ketiv/qere sits on the surrender clause the unit argues from.
rulings.grounds: All three arms verified. The prior addressee is Zedekiah, named in the relay clause כֹּ֥ה תֹאמְרֻ֖ן אֶל צִדְקִיָּֽהוּ (oshb:Jer.21.3, byte tier), with the oracle body addressing the defenders in the plural at 21:4; the named messengers are couriers. The shift at 21:8 is itself byte-true - the verse opens וְאֶל הָעָ֤ם הַזֶּה֙ תֹּאמַ֔ר כֹּ֖ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֑ה (oshb:Jer.21.8, byte tier), naming a new addressee - so the seam stands and only its stated point of departure is wrong; it is the same wording defect that stands in the preceding span's rejected alternative. On parity: that spliced run ends on the messenger formula while the gloss stops at the commission clause, “You shall say to this people” (web:Jer.21.8); the formula is rendered inside the same verse in the other witness, so the gap is this row's own cut and not the translation's - gloss extent must equal splice extent. On the variant: the inventory records a ketiv/qere at Jer.21.9 (1 note), the pair יחיה וְחָיָ֔ה (oshb:Jer.21.9, byte tier), unpointed ketiv then pointed qere, standing on the verb that governs the surrender outcome the row summarises as the terms of surrender and cites among its own evidence refs. No disclosure appears in any field, and no declared queue entry exists for this row because no quote binds to that verse, so the variant is neither declared nor examined on a verse whose content is argued in prose.
rulings.remedy: boundary_rationale: (a) correct the point of departure to Zedekiah and the defenders addressed in the plural, matching the edit made to the preceding span; (b) extend the English gloss so it covers the whole spliced run through the messenger formula, or shorten the splice to the clause the gloss already covers. device_notes: disclose the ketiv/qere at Jer.21.9 (single-witness). Test the cure must pass: gloss and splice must cover the same clause boundaries in the same field, the corrected addressee sentence must name the party the relay clause at 21:3 names, and every K/Q verse whose content is argued in prose must carry a disclosure even where no quote binds to it.

rulings.challenge_claim: The declared closure signal is positionally false at both cited sites, the ketiv/qere at 21:12 alternates precisely the addressee the unit's driver depends on, and a conjunctive onset plus an in-span messenger formula go unweighed.
rulings.grounds: All three arms verified on bytes. Neither cited occurrence is verse-final: at 21:13 the formula stands at words 7-8 of 15 and the verse runs on to its closing question, and at 21:14 it stands at words 5-6 of 12, the verse ending on וְהִצַּ֤תִּי אֵשׁ֙ בְּיַעְרָ֔הּ וְאָכְלָ֖ה כָּל סְבִיבֶֽיהָ (oshb:Jer.21.14, byte tier). Across 21:7, 21:10, 21:13, 21:14 and 22:5 every occurrence is clause-internal, five of five. The ruled reading of this formula is closure corroboration only where a fresh tier-1 onset follows: that holds for 21:14, followed by the commissioning imperative at 22:1, and not for 21:13, which is mid-span. So the closes-twice statement is false as a positional claim and half-false as a closure claim. On the variant: the inventory records a ketiv/qere at Jer.21.12 (1 note), מעלליהם מַעַלְלֵיכֶֽם (oshb:Jer.21.12, byte tier), a third-person-plural ketiv against a second-person-plural qere on the deeds, standing verse-final, with כִּפְרִ֥י מַעַלְלֵיכֶ֖ם (oshb:Jer.21.14, byte tier) unvaried on the qere side. The declared disposition is right on its quote-binding arm - the spliced vocative is verse-initial - but the row's filed driver is the addressee shift and the variant alternates exactly that, so a false positive on quote-binding is not a false positive on the driver. On the onsets: the span opens on וּלְבֵית֙ (oshb:Jer.21.11, byte tier), vav-prefixed and lamed-topical, a conjunctive opening left unweighed against the fresh-address claim; and כֹּ֚ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה (oshb:Jer.21.12, byte tier) stands inside the span without appearing among the filed signals, unlike the adjacent spans at 21:8-21:10 and 22:1-22:9, which file it.
rulings.remedy: boundary_rationale: replace the statement that the oracle closes on the formula twice with a positionally true one - both occurrences are clause-internal, and only the 21:14 occurrence corroborates closure, because a fresh tier-1 onset follows at 22:1; weigh the vav-prefixed conjunctive opening at 21:11 against the fresh-address claim in the same field. observed_substrate_signals: add the messenger-formula key for the in-span occurrence at 21:12, then re-check the dependent fields the driver set governs - unit_type, confidence and strongest_rejected_alternative. device_notes: disclose the ketiv/qere at Jer.21.12 (single-witness) and state that it alternates the addressee the row's driver turns on. Test the cure must pass: no closure claim may assert a verse-final position the verse's own bytes contradict, and a declared false positive may be closed only on the arm it was declared for.

rulings.challenge_claim: Both lenses land on the same defect: the rejected alternative's ground, that the messenger-formula restart at 22:6 reopens without a change of frame-owner or addressee, is contradicted by the bytes and by the unit's own rationale sentence. One lens adds that high confidence is not supported once the shift is accounted for and proposes the personification pattern as the better warrant; the other adds an unweighed break at the declined juncture and two undisclosed ketiv/qere verses.
rulings.grounds: Same core defect reached independently by both lenses; the added arms are distinct, and the core is upheld. At 22:1 the house is the destination of a commission, רֵ֖ד בֵּֽית מֶ֣לֶךְ יְהוּדָ֑ה (oshb:Jer.22.1, byte tier), with no preposition, and 22:2 addresses the king himself, שְׁמַ֣ע דְּבַר יְהוָ֔ה מֶ֣לֶךְ יְהוּדָ֔ה (oshb:Jer.22.2, byte tier), in the singular, אַתָּ֤ה וַעֲבָדֶ֨יךָ֙ (oshb:Jer.22.2, byte tier). At 22:6 the same three-word phrase returns under ayin-lamed, עַל בֵּית֙ מֶ֣לֶךְ יְהוּדָ֔ה (oshb:Jer.22.6, byte tier), and the address is to the house itself, גִּלְעָ֥ד אַתָּ֛ה לִ֖י (oshb:Jer.22.6, byte tier), continued at 22:7 in מִבְחַ֣ר אֲרָזֶ֔יךָ (oshb:Jer.22.7, byte tier). The phrase is a 7-verse object at consonantal tier (sweep: 7 verses: 21:11, 22:1, 22:6, 27:18, 27:21, 32:2, 38:22) and this span carries two of its members under two different frames. The row's own boundary_rationale states the same turn from the reigning king to the house itself, so the rejected alternative contradicts its own unit as well as the bytes. One added arm needs refining: the shift is not cleanly plural-to-singular, since 22:2's own verb and pronoun are singular and the plural forms stand at 22:3, 22:4 and 22:5; the byte-true description is a change of referent carried by the preposition, not by grammatical number alone. The other added arms hold: the SAMEKH recorded at Jer.22.5 falls after that verse, at exactly the 22:5|22:6 juncture the alternative declines, disclosed in one field and left unweighed in the field it bears on (single-witness, tier-3 weak, never a driver); and two ketiv/qere verses sit inside the span, one note each at Jer.22.4, ועבדו וַעֲבָדָ֖יו (oshb:Jer.22.4, byte tier), inside the promise clause the row paraphrases, and one at Jer.22.6, verse-final - neither disclosed, and only the 22:6 one standing in the declared queue, whose narrow quote-binding arm is confirmed since the quoted English stops well before the variant. High confidence with the frontier flag unset is not supported while the stated ground is byte-contradicted at the juncture it declines. The cut itself is not decided here.
rulings.remedy: strongest_rejected_alternative: replace the no-change-of-frame-owner-or-addressee ground with the byte-true one - the frame-owner does not change, but the addressee does, from the king addressed at 22:2 to the house addressed at 22:6 under a different preposition - and keep the span whole on the personification pattern, weighing and explicitly declining the disclosed break after Jer.22.5 in that same field. confidence: lower from high to medium. device_notes: disclose the ketiv/qere at Jer.22.4 and at Jer.22.6 (single-witness, one note each). Do not change the span: a split at 22:5|22:6 is a boundary PROPOSAL requiring explicit adoption, never author work. Test the cure must pass: the rewritten ground must not deny a shift the row's own boundary_rationale asserts, it must survive the check that killed the original - the preposition and address contrast between 22:1-22:2 and 22:6-22:7, visible in both witnesses - and every K/Q verse inside the span must be disclosed whether or not a quote binds to it.

rulings.challenge_claim: A verse-initial messenger formula inside the span is left out of the filed signals, the setumah that divides the span is reported without its internal force, and the type-guess supplies an identification the bytes do not carry.
rulings.grounds: The first arm is upheld: 22:11 opens on כִּ֣י כֹ֣ה אָֽמַר יְ֠הוָה (oshb:Jer.22.11, byte tier), a verse-initial ki-subordinated messenger formula absent from the filed signals, although the same shape is filed for the adjacent spans at 20:1-20:6, 21:1-21:7, 21:8-21:10 and 22:1-22:9. The ki subordinates, so cohesion holds and the cut at 22:9|22:10 is not in doubt. The second arm is overstated. The inventory does record SAMEKH at Jer.22.10, a break after that verse dividing the three-verse span, but the field already carries the within-the-span wording that the same construction is faulted for lacking elsewhere in this part; what remains is only that the break is attributed to the opening verse without saying it separates 22:10 from 22:11-22:12 - a wording correction, not a missing disclosure (single-witness, tier-3 weak, never a driver). The third arm is upheld on both counts: the spliced run from 22:11 stops at the royal title while the gloss runs on through הַמֹּלֵךְ֙ תַּ֚חַת יֹאשִׁיָּ֣הוּ אָבִ֔יו (oshb:Jer.22.11, byte tier), so gloss extent exceeds splice extent; and the type field reads the unnamed dead of 22:10 as Josiah, whom 22:10-22:12 never identify as the dead - he appears there only as Shallum's father and as the king Shallum reigned in place of. A byte-unsupported identification in a row field carries the same discipline as a digit.
rulings.remedy: observed_substrate_signals: add the messenger-formula key for the verse-initial occurrence at 22:11, then re-check the dependent fields the driver set governs - unit_type, confidence and strongest_rejected_alternative. device_notes: state that the SAMEKH recorded at Jer.22.10 falls after that verse and therefore separates 22:10 from 22:11-22:12 within the span. boundary_rationale: extend the splice from 22:11 through the reign clause so it covers the gloss, or shorten the gloss to the royal title the splice ends on. literature_type_guess: remove the identification of the dead as Josiah and describe the contrast the verses do carry - no weeping for the dead, weeping for the one who goes away, resolved at 22:11 to Shallum. Test the cure must pass: gloss and splice must cover the same clause boundaries, and no row field may name a referent the span's own verses leave unnamed.
